meta.title: Spinoza says free will is an illusion — and that frees you

plates.query: Jacob van Ruisdael View of Haarlem landscape sky
plates.want: Ruisdael, vast nature under an immense sky (PD)

plates.query: Vincent van Gogh Starry Night over the Rhone

beats.text: A stone thrown through the air, Spinoza said, would swear it chose to fly.
It feels the motion, not the hand that threw it — so it calls the motion its own free will.
We are that stone. We feel our wants, but not the long chain of causes behind them.
For Spinoza there is no will floating free of nature. Everything follows by necessity, like geometry.
This sounds like a prison. He said it is the opposite — it is the only door out.
Freedom is not escaping the causes. It is understanding them clearly enough to stop raging against them.
Stop fighting what had to be. See the whole, and a strange calm takes the place of blame.

source_note: Ideas from the Ethics, trans. R. H. M. Elwes (1883, public domain) — paraphrased.
